cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 49 since December 7, 2020. Law enforcement officer with the Shelby County Sheriff's Office. Auburn graduate (criminal justice, 1998) with a Troy University master's degree (2005). Wikipedia says he also served on the Alabaster City Council.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Russell Bedsole was born or raised, or when he moved to Alabama. The pages we could read did not show which bills he sponsored, so we could not document specific actions on the issues voters ask about. We found no public statements from him on data centers, development, homestead taxes, land ownership by investors or foreign buyers, immigration or H-1B, school choice or teacher pay, or policing and pensions. His campaign site says taxes should be kept low and not regressive and that students and schools need full support, but gives no specifics, so we left those out. Sources disagree on whether he is a captain or a major at the sheriff's office, and on the name of his Troy University degree. We found no endorsements, news controversies or foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and the legislator scorecards listed there were not readable in detail.
